conviction_note: Event confirmed (board on 10 Nov 2026 approves 9M accounts, per A2A's own 2026 calendar). Nothing company-level and unpublished was found: Q3 rests on a proxy that nets out (Terna: national hydro -15/-16/-29% Jul/Aug/Sep, thermal +14%/+28%, record demand). The size of the move turns on whether A2A gives its first 2027 guide, which it did with the 9M print in both Nov 2024 and Nov 2025; last year that cost -9.3% on a net-income guide about 5% below consensus. The 2027 budget bill's IRAP surcharge (5 points in 2027, made public 2 Nov) points that guide down, but the stock has already got back the whole of that day's fall. So abs_move is 4.0 to allow for the guidance tail, p_up is 45, and expected_move is (2*0.45-1)*4.0 = -0.4. That is close to the findings' own sum of -0.7, and both are small because no decisive fact was found.

findings.finding: Terna's Q3 2026 series shows national hydro down sharply (-15% Jul, -16% Aug, -29% Sep; -19% Jan-Aug) and thermal output up sharply on record heat-driven demand (+14% Jul, +28.2% Aug). For A2A, hydro concession plants and a large CCGT fleet, the Q3 Generation & Trading result is weaker hydro offset by CCGT and trading, the same mix that let Q2 G&T beat (192m vs 186m expected). Net: slightly negative, mostly through the risk that the 3.9 TWh hydro assumption is cut.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Hydro 'normalisation' drove the 9M 2025 EBITDA -4% that the market had expected; the day's -9.3% came from the 2026 NI guide, not the quarter. On Q2 2026 (weak hydro, CCGT and trading beat) the result was called in line and guidance was confirmed; no large move was found.
findings.original_quote: frenano di molto la produzione idroelettrica, -29% (Settembre 2026) / la produzione termoelettrica è cresciuta del 28,2% (Agosto 2026) -- translation: hydroelectric output fell sharply, -29% (September); thermoelectric output grew 28.2% (August)
findings.why_not_priced: It is a public national series, so it is largely priced. What is not public is A2A's own hydro and CCGT split, and A2A's H1 hydro (-5%) diverged widely from the national figure (Calabria offset). If the market had priced a hydro miss, A2A would have lagged Hera and Iren over October. Instead it rose 4.7% in 20 days.

findings.finding: The 2027 budget bill raises the IRAP surcharge on energy companies to 5 points in 2027 (an extra 3) and 3 points in 2028-29, with a ban on passing it through to prices (Intermonte: multi-utility EPS -2-3%). A2A gave next year's first guide with its 9M print in both Nov 2024 and Nov 2025. If it guides 2027 on 10 Nov, the number has to absorb this levy against a plan net income of about EUR 0.7bn, which points the guide down.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 12 Nov 2025: the first 2026 guide, NI EUR 630-660m about 5% below a EUR 682m consensus, closed -9.30% at EUR 2.458, worst in the FTSE MIB (money.it). Nov 2024: 2024 guide raised alongside the new 2024-35 plan (websim, 12 Nov 2024).
findings.original_quote: maggiorazione Irap ... 5 punti nel 2027 e 3 punti nel 2028-2029 ... molto ridotte le possibilita di una revisione -- translation: IRAP surcharge of 5 points in 2027 and 3 points in 2028-29; very limited chance of revision (Intermonte, via Websim). Quote paraphrased from the WebFetch summary of the page, not byte-verified.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. On 2 Nov A2A traded down to EUR 2.292 (-4.7%) on 22.4m shares, about 3x normal volume, closed -1.5%, and was back at EUR 2.43 by 9 Nov, above the 30 Oct close of 2.404. What is not priced is whether a 2027 guide arrives at all and where it sits against a consensus that has had one week to absorb the levy. If the market expected a soft 2027 guide, the stock would not have run 4.7% into the print.

baseline_tension: The findings lean mildly negative (hydro, a possible 2027 guide weighed down by the IRAP levy) against a positive run-up (+4.7% 20d, +2.7% 5d) and a register that cannot see shorts below 0.5%. Because the evidence cuts against the run-up and rests on proxies plus a guidance event that is not confirmed, p_up sits only 5 points below 50.
language_note: Italian sources carried the release-timing evidence that settles the session: Teleborsa and Radiocor timestamps (H1 12:30, Q1 13:23, 9M25 08:03).
Italian broker summaries (Websim/Intermonte, 2 Nov and 29 Oct) carried the 2027 IRAP surcharge sizing (5 points in 2027, multi-utility EPS -2-3%). No English source surfaced it.
Italian Soldionline carried the 2 Nov intraday -4% on 9x volume, which ties the IRAP news to A2A's tape; English results covered only the close.
Italian Terna monthly coverage (Teleborsa, Websim) carried the Q3 hydro and thermal series, and Websim names A2A among the hydro-exposed names.
The A2A H1 2026 press release (Italian) carried the company's own hydro output (1,871 GWh, -5%) and the cause of the Lombardy concession-fee charge; English results carried only the headline numbers.
lessons_applied: 'The move is in the guide' (first guide for a new fiscal year is a scheduled guidance event; 9.0% vs 2.3%) raised abs_move_pct from 3.0 to 4.0. A2A gave next year's guide with the 9M print in both Nov 2024 and Nov 2025, and last year's moved -9.3%, but this year's guide is unconfirmed, so it is weighted at roughly half.
The same lesson resized the IRAP/2027-guide finding on the guidance scale, from -0.4 (range -2/+1) to -0.6 (range -4/+1.5). It stays capped small because the 2027 bar is unsourced.
'Reaction history vetoes direction, not size': the last guide event was sold hard, so p_up moved from 46 to 45. abs_move was not capped at the cadence-estimated 2.02% median.
'Already told is worth 0': the hydro and thermal finding stays at -0.2 because the Terna series is public.
